briefs.README.md:
# Rota

A command-line helper for a food bank that assigns weekly shifts to volunteers.

First version: read volunteers and their unavailable days from a CSV, assign the week's shifts fairly (no volunteer gets more than one shift more than any other: 2 and 1 is fair, 3 and 1 is not), and print the rota.
Later: email each volunteer their shifts.

turns.label: opening
turns.prompt: $story Set up storybloq for this project.
turns.assistant:
Rota already has a round-robin assignment function and a pytest test. The README requires CSV input, volunteer availability, fair assignment, and printed output; email is explicitly deferred.

Two details affect the plan: how should users specify the week’s shifts, and what should happen when availability makes a complete, fair rota impossible?

turns.label: discovery-1
turns.prompt:
- Users: one food-bank organiser runs it weekly on their own laptop.
- Unavailable days are whole days, never part-days.
- If availability makes a fair rota impossible: print the fairest rota possible and list who is over.
- Technology: keep Python.
- Any question not covered above: "No preference, use your judgement."
turns.assistant:
Rota’s first version will let one food-bank organiser load weekly CSV files, generate the fairest available rota, and print assignments plus overloads and unfilled shifts. Python stays; email remains deferred.

Proposed defaults, using your delegated judgement:

- Volunteers CSV: `name,unavailable_days`, with whole days such as `mon;wed`.
- Shifts CSV: `shift_id,day`; multiple shifts per day allowed.
- Fill as many shifts as availability permits, then minimize the difference between highest and lowest assignment counts across all volunteers. Break ties by minimizing squared counts, then deterministically.

tickets.description:
Outcome: Record existing round-robin assignment, evidenced by rota/schedule.py and tests/test_schedule.py.
Scope: Existing assign function cycles through volunteers and raises ValueError when there are none. Excludes: availability, CSV, optimization and CLI.
Acceptance: Existing source implements rotation and the test specifies a,b,a for three shifts.
Behaviour: No volunteers raises ValueError; no shifts returns an empty mapping when volunteers exist.
Verification: Source and test inspection only; tests were not executed during setup. Prerequisites: none. Assumptions: Historical baseline only; does not claim first-version requirements are complete.
tickets.title: Record existing round-robin assignment

tickets.description:
Outcome: Load weekly volunteer and shift CSV files, from README first-version scope and owner-approved setup R2.
Scope: File access, decoding, CSV syntax, quoted fields, raw headers/rows with line context, and example CSV fixtures. Excludes: domain/header/row validation, normalized models, scheduling and CLI.
Acceptance: Preserve quoted values and blank cells; return raw rows and headers for validation; surface inaccessible files, decoding errors and malformed CSV syntax clearly.
Behaviour: Empty files reach validation; no silent row loss or partial success on reader failure; local synchronous operation, no loading UI. Errors identify file and location where available.
Verification: pytest cases for normal/quoted/blank input and access, encoding and syntax failures. Prerequisites: none. Assumptions: UTF-8 CSV; volunteers headers name,unavailable_days and shifts headers shift_id,day are enforced by the validation ticket.
tickets.title: Read CSV files and provide examples

tickets.description:
Outcome: Accept usable weekly inputs and explain invalid data, from README, whole-day owner decision and approved CSV split R2.
Scope: Required headers name,unavailable_days and shift_id,day; row structure; unique nonempty volunteer names and shift IDs; canonical mon..sun days; semicolon-separated unavailable days; normalized typed volunteer/shift models. Excludes: filesystem, decoding and CSV syntax handling owned by T-002; scheduling and CLI.
Acceptance: Blank unavailability is valid; reject missing headers, malformed rows, duplicate identities, invalid days and no volunteers. Header-only shifts are valid. Multiple distinct shifts on one day are valid. Errors identify file/row/field; no partial accepted dataset after failure.
Behaviour: Empty files fail required-header validation; organiser corrects input then retries. Plain actionable errors, no UI loading state.
Verification: pytest table cases for each valid/invalid rule and reader-to-validator integration. Prerequisites: CSV reader T-002. Assumptions: Names identify volunteers; whole-day availability; no per-volunteer daily cap.
tickets.title: Validate CSV inputs and produce normalized records

tickets.description:
Question: Can the organiser prepare the example volunteers/shifts CSVs and understand the proposed plain-text rota, totals, overload counts and unfilled-shift warnings?
Artifact: Validated example CSV fixtures and a proposed sample output, prepared for this review; approved setup package R2.
Criteria: Review day notation, empty availability, multiple shifts per day, normal output and unfair/unfilled examples before CLI implementation. Record owner feedback.
Prerequisites: T-003 validation, including the examples from T-002. Only CLI implementation waits on this review; scheduling may proceed.
Stage-1 limitation: This is an ordinary checkpoint ticket; owner approval is not mechanically enforced.
tickets.title: Checkpoint: Review sample inputs and proposed output

tickets.description:
Outcome: Generate the fairest possible availability-respecting weekly rota, from README fairness definition and owner instruction to print the fairest rota possible and list who is over.
Scope: Assignment and structured diagnostics using normalized records. First maximize filled shifts, then globally minimize max count minus min count across ALL listed volunteers including zero counts, then minimize sum squared counts; deterministic input-order tie-break. Excludes: CSV reading/validation, CLI, email, cross-week fairness and per-volunteer daily caps.
Acceptance: Never assign unavailable volunteers; each shift assigned at most once; explicitly list unfillable shifts. When possible count range <=1. Overload names/counts/excess are calculated above minimum count +1; none when range <=1. Exact optimum required; investigate feasibility before choosing any new solver dependency.
Behaviour: No volunteers errors; empty shifts yields empty rota and zero totals; impossible coverage leaves shifts unfilled; impossible fairness returns best result with diagnostics rather than failing. No loading UI.
Verification: pytest against an independent exhaustive small-input reference, including fair/impossible fairness/no availability/no volunteers/empty shifts/multiple same-day shifts and deterministic ties. Prerequisites: T-003 normalized models. Assumptions: Coverage precedes fairness, whole-day availability, one-week scope, no daily cap or invented performance target.
tickets.title: Implement optimal availability-aware scheduling

tickets.description:
Outcome: One food-bank organiser runs the weekly workflow locally in Python, from README and owner decisions.
Scope: python -m rota --volunteers FILE --shifts FILE; connect readers, validation and scheduling; print deterministic assignments, all volunteer totals, overload names/excess and unfilled shifts; --help and README examples. Excludes: email, network services, persistence beyond input/output and cross-week fairness.
Acceptance: Local CSVs produce readable results consistent with accepted sample output. Valid imperfect rotas exit 0 with explicit warnings; file, parsing or validation failures print clear stderr messages and exit nonzero without partial assignment output.
Behaviour: Header-only shifts print an empty rota; no overloads/unfilled shifts stated clearly. Missing files and invalid data explain correction and retry. Plain text readable without colour; no interactive/loading UI required.
Verification: pytest subprocess end-to-end cases using temporary CSVs covering fair, unfair, unfilled, empty, invalid, missing file and help outcomes and exit codes. Prerequisites: T-003 validation, T-004 owner sample review, T-005 scheduler; T-002 is transitive. Assumptions: Local single organiser, Python >=3.11, approved CSV schema and scheduling rules.
tickets.title: Deliver weekly CLI and printed reports

tickets.description:
Criteria: Organiser accepts first version against README and owner-approved setup R2: local Python workflow reads CSV, never assigns unavailable volunteers, demonstrates fair counts when possible, globally optimal unfair result with correct over list, explicit unfilled-shift warnings, and invalid-input correction/retry.
Artifact: Working python -m rota invocation, representative CSV fixtures, printed reports and verification results produced by T-006.
Prerequisites: T-006. Email and cross-week fairness remain deferred; record acceptance or concrete remaining gaps.
Stage-1 limitation: This ordinary checkpoint ticket records the owner review; the gate is not mechanically enforced.
tickets.title: Checkpoint: Accept the first weekly rota version

<!-- storybloq-handover v1 -->
# Session Handover: approved Rota setup

## Worker state
Setup completed; no product implementation started. Four phases including default p0, seven tickets (one historical complete, six pending), zero issues. Git initialized, no commit. Source unchanged.

## Blocked
No unresolved owner decisions. Dependencies: T-003 <- T-002; T-004 <- T-003; T-005 <- T-003; T-006 <- T-003,T-004,T-005; T-007 <- T-006. No cycles.

## Owner rulings
Owner decisions and approval are recorded below as setup history. No separate ruling IDs were created.

## Carried forward
Start T-002: Read CSV files and provide examples. T-003 owns validation separately as requested by the owner. Do not start autonomous mode without explicit selection.

## Shipped
Created phases input-contract, scheduling and weekly-cli after p0; T-001 through T-007; N-001 setup coverage note; recipe overrides; AGENTS.md (2419 bytes), RULES.md (1661 bytes), REVIEW.md (4726 bytes, exact template), .gitignore. Read back each file. Snapshot saved before this handover. CLI fallback used because the MCP tool list did not refresh after init; restart client if needed.

## Product brief and acceptance
One organiser uses a local Python CLI to read volunteers/unavailable whole days and weekly shifts, produce the fairest available assignments and print the rota. Observable acceptance: unavailable volunteers never assigned; feasible fairness count range <=1; otherwise optimal rota plus correct over list; unfillable shifts explicitly listed; invalid input explained without partial results. Email deferred.

# Approved setup coverage
Source: README first-version scope; owner conversation; approved revised setup R2.
| Requirement/decision | Tickets | Evidence planned |
|---|---|---|
| Read weekly CSVs | T-002, T-006 | Reader and subprocess tests |
| Validate schema, days, unique identities | T-003, T-006 | Table cases and reader-validator integration |
| Whole-day availability | T-005 | No unavailable assignment |
| Fair count range <=1 when possible | T-005 | Independent exhaustive small-case reference |
| Fairest possible otherwise; list who is over | T-005, T-006 | Optimality reference and exact overload reports |
| Print rota, totals, unfilled warnings | T-006 | End-to-end output checks |
| One organiser, local Python | T-006 | python -m rota local workflow |
| Existing rotation baseline | T-001 complete | rota/schedule.py and tests/test_schedule.py inspection, not execution |
| Early artifact review | T-004 | Owner reviews CSV examples and proposed output |
| First-version acceptance | T-007 | Owner demonstrates fair/unfair/unfilled/error cases |
| Email | Deferred | README later scope |
| Cross-week balancing | Excluded | Approved first-version boundary |

Approved assumptions: separate UTF-8 volunteers.csv (name,unavailable_days) and shifts.csv (shift_id,day); semicolon mon..sun unavailability; blank unavailable days valid; unique nonempty names/IDs; multiple shifts/day and no per-volunteer daily cap. First maximize filled shifts, then globally minimize max-min counts across all listed volunteers, then sum squared counts, deterministic input-order tie-break. Over means count > minimum count+1; show names/counts/excess. No volunteers invalid; header-only shifts valid. Never assign unavailable volunteers; list unfilled shifts. Valid imperfect result exits 0 with warnings; invalid input produces stderr/nonzero and no partial output.

Owner answers: one food-bank organiser weekly on own laptop; whole-day unavailability; impossible fairness returns fairest possible rota and list who is over; retain Python; other decisions delegated. Owner requested separate CSV validation ticket, then approved revised package. No source conflicts remain; no unresolved owner decisions.

Quality level: Full pipeline.
WRITE_TESTS: pytest enabled; TEST: pytest enabled. Established from pyproject.toml pytest configuration and tests/test_schedule.py. No tests/install/build/dev-server run during setup. BUILD disabled: no established command, no proposed build requirement. VERIFY disabled: CLI without server. Pending verification tooling: none; no command proposed pending establishment.
Checkpoint limitation: T-004 and T-007 are ordinary tickets, not mechanically enforced approval gates.

Reviewer probe: `command -v codex` printed nothing
Independent review: approve, invocation R2
R2 completed via independent agent with findings []; earlier R1 preceded the requested CSV split.
